You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

    if "[DEBUG" not in r.stderr:
        print(r.stderr[:2000])

    print("===")

run('source_type="json"\n')
run('base_address_shift=5\n')

PY

        open("/tmp/c.toml","w").write(cfg); args+=["-c","/tmp/c.toml"]
    args+=["--log","debug"]+extra
    r=subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True)

    pat=re.compile(r'"([^"]+)": IdentFormat \{\s+case: (?:Some\(\s+(\w+),?\s+\)|(None)),\s+prefix: "([^"]*)",\s+suffix: "([^"]*)",', re.S)

    r=subprocess.run(["./executable","-c","/tmp/c.toml","--log","debug"], capture_output=True, text=True)

run('[[settings.riscv_config.harts]]\n')
run('[settings.riscv_config]\nharts=[1,2]\n')
run('[settings.riscv_config]\nharts=["a"]\n')

import subprocess, os, shutil, filecmp, re, sys, json
ORIG="/workspace/executable"
OURS="/tmp/bin_ours/executable"
def run_one(binary, case, root):
    # root: work dir
    os.makedirs(root, exist_ok=True)
    out=os.path.join(root,"out"); os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    args=[]
    # case may define files to create in cwd: dict name->content
    for fname,content in (case.get("files") or {}).items():
        p=os.path.join(root,fname); os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True) if os.path.dirname(p)!=root else None
        open(p,"w").write(content)
    svd_path=None
    if "svd" in case:
        svd_path=os.path.join(root, case.get("svd_name","input.svd")); open(svd_path,"w").write(case["svd"])
    elif "svd_path" in case:
        svd_path=case["svd_path"]
    if not case.get("no_input_arg"):
        if svd_path: args+=["-i", svd_path]
    if not case.get("no_output_arg"):
        args+=["-o", out]
    args+=case.get("args",[])
    # Expand placeholders in args: {out},{cwd},{svd}
    args=[a.replace("{out}",out).replace("{cwd}",root).replace("{svd}",svd_path or "") for a in args]
    env={k:v for k,v in os.environ.items() if k not in ("RUST_LOG",)}
    env.update(case.get("env") or {})
    stdin_data=case.get("stdin")
    if isinstance(stdin_data,str): stdin_data=stdin_data.encode()
    r=subprocess.run([binary]+args, cwd=root, input=stdin_data, capture_output=True, env=env)
    # collect generated files in out plus any files generated in cwd (lib/mod/build/device/generic)
    files={}
    for base, prefix in [(out,"out/"),(root,"cwd/")]:
        if os.path.isdir(base):
            for fn in sorted(os.listdir(base)):
                fp=os.path.join(base,fn)
                if os.path.isfile(fp):
                    # exclude input/case files in cwd root
                    if prefix=="cwd/" and fn in (case.get("files") or {}): continue
                    if prefix=="cwd/" and svd_path and fp==svd_path: continue
                    if prefix=="cwd/" and fn not in ("lib.rs","mod.rs","build.rs","device.x","generic.rs"): continue
                    try: files[prefix+fn]=open(fp,"rb").read()
                    except: pass
    return {"rc":r.returncode,"stdout":r.stdout,"stderr":r.stderr,"files":files}

def normalize(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    # normalize thread id in panics: thread 'main' (123)
    b=re.sub(rb"thread 'main' \(\d+\)", b"thread 'main' (ID)", b)
    # panic locations src/...:line:col keep but will differ; for diff display only
    return b

def compare_case(case, verbose=False):
    name=case["name"]
    base=f"/tmp/cmp/{name}"
    shutil.rmtree(base,ignore_errors=True)
    ro=run_one(ORIG,case,base+"/orig")
    ru=run_one(OURS,case,base+"/ours")
    ok=True; msgs=[]
    if ro["rc"]!=ru["rc"]: ok=False; msgs.append(f"rc orig={ro['rc']} ours={ru['rc']}")
    if normalize(ro["stdout"])!=normalize(ru["stdout"]): ok=False; msgs.append(f"stdout diff orig={ro['stdout'][:500]!r} ours={ru['stdout'][:500]!r}")
    # Sort identFormats debug? debug logs are nondeterministic ordering in both; if log debug in args/env, compare stderr non-debug lines only? Keep raw but note.
    if normalize(ro["stderr"])!=normalize(ru["stderr"]):
        ok=False
        # show first diff
        so=normalize(ro["stderr"]).decode(errors="replace").splitlines(); su=normalize(ru["stderr"]).decode(errors="replace").splitlines()
        import difflib
        diff=list(difflib.unified_diff(so,su,"orig.stderr","ours.stderr",lineterm=""))
        msgs.append("stderr diff:\n"+"\n".join(diff[:60]))
    allfiles=set(ro["files"])|set(ru["files"])
    for f in sorted(allfiles):
        if ro["files"].get(f)!=ru["files"].get(f):
            ok=False
            if f not in ro["files"]: msgs.append(f"file {f} only in ours ({len(ru['files'][f])} bytes)")
            elif f not in ru["files"]: msgs.append(f"file {f} only in orig ({len(ro['files'][f])} bytes)")
            else:
                so=ro["files"][f].decode(errors="replace").splitlines(); su=ru["files"][f].decode(errors="replace").splitlines()
                import difflib
                diff=list(difflib.unified_diff(so,su,f"orig/{f}",f"ours/{f}",lineterm=""))
                msgs.append(f"file {f} diff ({len(diff)} lines):\n"+"\n".join(diff[:80]))
    print(("PASS " if ok else "FAIL ")+name)
    if not ok:
        for m in msgs: print(m)
    return ok

def safety(name, fields, size=8):

fn emit_register_traces(per_name:&str, items:&[RegisterCluster], _config:&Config) {
    // Original trace in peripheral::render at checking derivation and expanding phases has complex order; output only matters at trace level.
    fn walk(items:&[RegisterCluster], per_name:&str, path:&[String]) {
        for rc in items {
            match rc {
                RegisterCluster::Register(r)=>{
                    let derive_str = match &r.derived_from {
                        Some(df)=>{
                            let block_path = if path.is_empty() { format!("BlockPath {{ peripheral: \"{}\", path: [] }}", per_name) } else { format!("BlockPath {{ peripheral: \"{}\", path: {:?} }}", per_name, path) };
                            format!("Explicit(RegisterPath {{ block: {}, name: \"{}\" }})", block_path, df)
                        }
                        None=>"Root".into()
                    };
                    log::trace!("Register: {}, DeriveInfo: {}", r.name, derive_str);
                }
                RegisterCluster::Cluster(c)=>{
                    let mut p=path.to_vec(); p.push(c.name.clone()); walk(&c.children, per_name, &p);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    walk(items, per_name, &[]);
}

fn peripheral_instances(per:&Peripheral) -> Vec<(String,u64)> {
    if let Some(dim)=per.dim.dim {
        let indices=per.dim.indices().unwrap_or_default();
        let incr=per.dim.dim_increment.unwrap_or(0) as u64;
        let _=dim;
        indices.iter().enumerate().map(|(i,idx)| (expand_dim_name(&per.name, idx), per.base_address + (i as u64)*incr)).collect()
    } else { vec![(per.name.clone(), per.base_address)] }
}

fn feature_token(per:&Peripheral, config:&Config, inst_name:&str) -> Option<(TokenStream,String)> {
    // feature_group: use group_name as feature; feature_peripheral: use peripheral name as feature
    // feature name formatting type peripheral_feature applied to group/peripheral name string
    if config.feature_peripheral {
        let fname=util::ident_str(inst_name, config, "peripheral_feature");
        Some((quote!{ #[cfg(feature=#fname)] }, fname))
    } else if config.feature_group {
        if let Some(g)=&per.group_name { let fname=util::ident_str(g, config, "peripheral_feature"); Some((quote!{ #[cfg(feature=#fname)] }, fname)) } else { None }
    } else { None }
}

fn render_singleton(per:&Peripheral, inst_name:&str, addr:u64, desc:&str, mod_ident:&Ident, config:&Config, _device:&Device) -> TokenStream {
    let ty=util::ident(inst_name, config, "peripheral");
    let spec=util::ident(inst_name, config, "peripheral_spec");
    let ty_str=ty.to_string();
    let addr_lit=util::hex_literal(addr);
    let feature_cfg = feature_token(per,config,inst_name).map(|(t,_)| t).unwrap_or_else(|| quote!{});
    // docs with html
    let doc_tokens = if let Some(url)=&config.settings.html_url {
        let see=format!("See peripheral [structure]({}#{})", url, inst_name);
        quote!{ #[doc=#desc] #[doc=""] #[doc=#see] }
    } else { quote!{ #[doc=#desc] } };
    quote!{
        #feature_cfg
        #doc_tokens
        pub type #ty = crate::Periph<#spec>;
        pub struct #spec;
        impl crate::PeripheralSpec for #spec { type RB = #mod_ident::RegisterBlock; const ADDRESS: usize = #addr_lit; const NAME: &'static str = #ty_str; }
    }
}
fn make_singleton_info(inst_name:&str, config:&Config, per:&Peripheral) -> Singleton {
    Singleton{ doc_name: inst_name.to_string(), field_ident: util::ident(inst_name, config, "peripheral_singleton"), ty_ident: util::ident(inst_name, config, "peripheral"), feature: feature_token(per,config,inst_name).map(|(t,_)| t) }
}

    #[derive(Clone)]

                        root_name=Some(target.name().to_string()); break;
                    } else { break; }

        infos.push(info);

                let (base_ty,base_mod,_)=rc_type_and_name(rc, ctx.config);

                        out.extend(quote!{ #[doc=#ddesc] pub use #base_ty as #der_ty; pub use #base_mod as #der_mod; });
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

fn html_for_register(ctx:&BlockContext, reg_name:&str) -> Option<String> {
    ctx.config.settings.html_url.as_ref().map(|url| format!("{}#{}:{}", url, ctx.html_path, reg_name))
}

fn render_cluster(c:&ClusterInfo, defaults:&RegisterProperties, ctx:&BlockContext) -> anyhow::Result<TokenStream> {
    let child_defaults=c.properties.merge(defaults);
    let (ty,mod_ident,name_for_type)=rc_type_and_name(&RegisterCluster::Cluster(c.clone()), ctx.config);
    let _=name_for_type;
    let desc=c.description.as_deref().map(util::clean_description).unwrap_or_else(|| c.name.clone());
    let child_ctx=BlockContext{ device:ctx.device, config:ctx.config, path:format!("{}.{}", ctx.path, c.name), html_path:format!("{}:{}", ctx.html_path, c.name) };
    // nested child modules
    let child_modules=render_child_modules(&c.children, &child_defaults, &child_ctx)?;
    // block struct for cluster
    let block=render_block_struct(&c.children, &child_defaults, &child_ctx, BlockStructKind::Cluster{ ty:&ty, desc:&desc, orig_name:&c.name }, Some(c))?;
    let alias_attr=if util::ident_str(&name_without_dim(&c.name), ctx.config, "cluster") != name_without_dim(&c.name) { let a=name_without_dim(&c.name); quote!{ #[doc(alias=#a)] } } else { quote!{} };
    // block returns struct+impl tokens including alias? We'll incorporate struct definition inside render_block_struct for cluster, which includes doc/alias.
    Ok(quote!{
        #[doc=#desc] pub use self::#mod_ident::#ty;
        #[doc=r"Cluster"]
        #[doc=#desc]
        pub mod #mod_ident {
            #block
            #child_modules
        }
    })
}

enum BlockStructKind<'a> {
    Peripheral,
    Cluster{ ty:&'a Ident, desc:&'a str, orig_name:&'a str },
